It would be comical if it weren’t so tragic.” “华盛顿有多位重要的中国企业首席执行官在场外观望，心里都在想：‘会不会叫到我？’”欧亚集团的中国问题高级分析师、曾在中国工作的前美国外交官杰里米·陈（音）说。“整件事太疯狂了。要不是因为太可悲，这件事甚至显得有点滑稽。” There was another complication: Some prominent Chinese companies face U.S. restrictions, making their appearance at a White House state dinner politically fraught. In June, the U.S. Department of Defense had included Alibaba and BYD in its expanded list of firms it identified as “ Chinese military companies .” 还有另一个复杂因素：一些中国知名企业受到美国方面的限制，相关企业的负责人如果出现在白宫国宴上，在政治上会相当棘手。今年6月，美国国防部把阿里巴巴和比亚迪列入了扩大后的所谓“ 中国军工企业 ”名单。 “It would actually be seen by some in Washington as provocative to bring these companies along,” said Ilaria Mazzocco, a deputy director at the Center for Strategic and International Studies specializing in Chinese business and economics. 专门研究中国商业和经济问题的战略与国际研究中心副主任伊拉里娅·马佐科说：“让这些公司参与进来实际上会被华盛顿一些人视为挑衅。” The contrast was especially striking compared with the scene when Mr. Trump visited Beijing in May. 与特朗普今年5月访问北京时的场面相比，这种反差尤其鲜明。 Apple’s Tim Cook, Tesla’s Elon Musk and other executives of top American companies stood on the steps of Beijing’s Great Hall of the People just behind senior U.S. officials. Mr. Trump told Mr. Xi that he had brought “the greatest businessmen, the biggest, and I guess the best, in the world.” 苹果的蒂姆·库克、特斯拉的埃隆·马斯克以及其他美国顶尖企业的高管站在北京人民大会堂的台阶上，紧挨在美国高级官员身后。特朗普对中国领导人说，他带来了“世界上最伟大的商人，最了不起的，我想也是最优秀的”。 Mr. Trump added, “I didn’t want the second or the third in the company, I wanted only the top, and they’re here today to pay respects to you and to China.” 特朗普还说：“我不要公司的二三把手，我要第一把手，所以他们都来了，表示出对中国和对您的尊重。” 今年5月特朗普访问北京期间，时任苹果首席执行官的蒂姆·库克出席欢迎仪式。 On Thursday, many of the same executives from U.S. firms were present again . Alongside Mr. Cook and Mr. Musk were Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Amazon’s Jeff Bezos, OpenAI’s Mr. Altman, Microsoft’s Satya Nadella and General Motors’ Mary Barra. 周四，不少来自同一批美国企业的高管 再次出席 。与库克和马斯克一同在场的还有英伟达的黄仁勋、Meta的马克·扎克伯格、亚马逊的杰夫·贝索斯、OpenAI的奥特曼、微软的萨蒂亚·纳德拉和通用汽车的玛丽·博拉。 Earlier in the day, Mr. Xi said in a speech that China “welcomes American companies wanting to invest and do business there.” Then, in an apparent reference to the U.S. restrictions on Chinese firms operating in America, he added: “We hope Chinese companies are treated fairly here in the United States.” 当天早些时候，习近平在讲话中说，中国“欢迎美国企业来华投资兴业”。随后，他显然是暗指美国对中国企业在美运营的限制，又补充说：“希望美方公平对待中国企业。” While American companies have not given up on China, they are struggling to compete against its companies. American automakers have lost ground to Chinese electric vehicle makers. Apple faces intense competition from Huawei. Nike is battling increasingly popular Chinese brands. 虽然美国企业并没有放弃中国市场，但它们正越来越难以与中国企业竞争。美国汽车制造商已经在与中国电动汽车制造商的竞争中节节败退。苹果正面临华为的激烈竞争。耐克也在应对越来越受欢迎的中国品牌的挑战。 Yet China remains too large and too deeply embedded in global manufacturing for many American companies to ignore. A 2026 survey by the U.S.-China Business Council found that 80 percent of American companies still regarded the Chinese market as either “very important” or “important” because of its scale and industrial ecosystem. 但对许多美国企业来说，中国市场规模太大，而且与全球制造业嵌合太深，因此难以忽视。美中贸易全国委员会2026年的一项调查发现，80%的美国企业仍认为中国市场“非常重要”或“重要”，原因在于其市场规模和产业生态体系。 For Chinese companies, the calculation about the United States is increasingly different. Tariffs, political scrutiny, investment restrictions and national security rules have made entering or expanding in the United States far more difficult, particularly for companies in strategic industries. 对中国企业而言，是否进入美国市场的考量正越来越不同。关税、政治审查、投资限制和国家安全规定，使得进入美国或在美国扩张变得困难得多，尤其是对那些处于战略性行业的企业而言。 Joerg Wuttke, a partner at DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group, a Washington-based consultancy, said seeing so many American business executives “kissing Xi’s ring” underscored how lopsided the relationship had become. 华盛顿咨询公司奥尔布赖特石桥集团合伙人伍德克(Joerg Wuttke)说，如此多美国企业高管“向习近平俯首示好”，凸显出这段经济关系已经变得多么失衡。 “Is there anybody from China interested in doing business in America?” Mr. Wuttke said. “No, because it’s not possible. So why should they waste their time?” 伍德克说：“中国还有谁有兴趣去美国做生意吗？没有，因为不可能。那他们为什么还要浪费时间？” Ana Swanson和Lauren Hirsch对本文有报道贡献。 黄瑞黎( Sui-Lee Wee )是《纽约时报》东南亚分社社长，负责该地区11个国家的报道。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

title: 美驻华大使：特朗普曾提议向中国出售武器
description: 黄安伟2026年9月28日中国国家主席习近平上周对美国进行国事访问。中国是全球军事力量增长最快的国家。 Kenny Holston/The New York Times President Trump has asked Xi Jinping, the leader of China, whether he would like to buy American weapons, David Perdue, the American ambassador to China, said in a television interview on Sunday. 美国驻华大使庞德伟(David Perdue)在周日的电视采访中表示，特朗普总统曾询问中国领导人习近平是否愿意购买美国武器。 “President Trump continues to say, ‘Hey, we sell arms to other people around the world,’” Mr. Perdue said on “Fox News Sunday” while discussing the state visit by Mr. Xi to Washington last week. “He actually asked President Xi would he like to buy some at one point.” “特朗普总统一直说，‘嘿，我们向世界各地的其他人出售武器。’他实际上问过习主席，是否愿意买一些，”庞德伟在《福克斯周日新闻》上讨论习近平上周对华盛顿的国事访问时说。 Mr. Perdue did not give further details and did not reveal Mr. Xi’s reply. 庞德伟没有提供更多细节，也没有透露习近平的答复。 An admission that the American president offered to sell arms to China is extraordinary. The Communist-ruled nation is considered by most American policymakers and legislators of both parties to be the greatest military, economic and diplomatic rival of the United States — the only real challenger to America as a superpower. 承认美国总统曾提出向中国出售武器，这是极不寻常的。这个由共产党执政的国家被美国两党大多数政策制定者和立法者视为美国在军事、经济和外交上的最大对手——也是美国作为超级大国的唯一真正挑战者。 When asked for comment, the White House said through a U.S. official that the United States had no plans to sell arms to China. The State Department said in a statement that “U.S. law prohibits arms sales to China and there is no offer or plan to sell arms to China.” 在被要求置评时，白宫通过一名美国官员表示，美国没有向中国出售武器的计划。美国国务院在声明中表示，“美国法律禁止向中国出售武器，并且没有向中国出售武器的提议或计划。” The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment. 中国驻华盛顿大使馆没有立即回应置评请求。 China has the world’s fastest-growing military, and for decades U.S. officials across administrations, including in the current one, have warned of a potential military clash between the two nuclear-armed powers in the Asia-Pacific region, particularly over the island of Taiwan or China’s aggressive actions in territory claimed by U.S. allies in the South and East China Seas. 中国拥有世界上发展最快的军队，几十年来，包括现任政府在内的历届美国政府官员都曾警告，这两个核武大国之间在亚太地区可能发生军事冲突，特别是围绕台湾问题，或是由于中国在美国盟友声称拥有主权的南海和东海领土采取的强硬行动。 Chinese defense companies, with the approval of the Chinese government, are supporting adversaries of the United States, including Iran and Russia, by selling them dual-use equipment and satellite imagery, as well as planning the secret export of weapons, according to U.S. officials. The United States has imposed sanctions on some Chinese companies. 据美国官员称，在得到中国政府批准的情况下，中国国防企业正在通过出售军民两用设备和卫星图像，以及策划秘密出口武器，来支持包括伊朗和俄罗斯在内的美国对手。美国已经对部分中国企业实施了制裁。 The United States has been the dominant military power in the Asia-Pacific region, but that strength is fading relative to China’s, especially as the Trump administration diverts resources from the region for use in its war against Iran. In recent years, the U.S. defense industry has also struggled to manufacture weapons systems at a rate considered sufficient for global needs by American officials. 美国一直是亚太地区的主导军事力量，但相对于中国，这种力量正在衰退，尤其是随着特朗普政府将该地区的资源调往对伊朗的战争中。近年来，美国国防工业也一直难以按照美国官员认为能满足全球需求的速度来制造武器系统。 “If there was any ambiguity about whether President Trump views China as a security threat, this disclosure by @USAmbChina Perdue puts the question to rest,” Ryan Hass, a former career diplomat and White House national security official who is director of the China center at the Brookings Institution, wrote on social media. “如果说对于特朗普总统是否将中国视为安全威胁还存在含糊之处，那么@USAmbChina（美国驻华大使）庞德伟的这一披露让这个问题有了定论，”前职业外交官、白宫国家安全官员、布鲁金斯学会中国中心主任何瑞恩(Ryan Hass)在社交媒体上写道。 “Trump’s offer to sell weapons to China will be unsettling to American partners at the pointy edge of China’s spear,” he added. “特朗普向中国出售武器的提议将让处于中国矛头最前沿的美国合作伙伴感到不安，”他还说。 Those partners include the Philippines, Japan and Taiwan, the de facto independent island and democracy that the Chinese Communist Party seeks to rule. 这些合作伙伴包括菲律宾、日本和台湾，台湾是一个事实上的独立岛屿和民主政体，是中国共产党企图统治的对象。 Mr. Trump has been withholding a $14 billion sale of weapons to Taiwan, even though the U.S. government has been required by law since 1979 to send arms of a defensive nature to the island. The latest arms package was put together by State Department officials and was approved by congressional leaders early this year, but has since languished at the department, The New York Times reported. 特朗普一直搁置向台湾出售价值140亿美元的武器，尽管自1979年以来，美国政府在法律上被要求向该岛提供防御性武器。据《纽约时报》报道，最新的军售一揽子计划由国务院官员拟定，并在今年早些时候获得了国会领导人的批准，但此后便一直被搁置在国务院。 Senators sent a bipartisan letter in May to Mr. Trump urging him to move forward with the sales. On Wednesday, hours before Mr. Xi arrived in Washington, four Republican senators led by Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asking for the same thing. 今年5月，参议员们向特朗普发送了一封两党联名信，敦促他推进军售。周三，就在习近平抵达华盛顿前几个小时，由肯塔基州参议员米奇·麦康奈尔牵头的四位共和党参议员致信国务卿马可·鲁比奥和国防部长皮特·海格塞斯，提出了同样的要求。 They also pressed the two men to allocate $300 million in aid for purchasing arms that Congress had already approved for Taiwan, as well as $1 billion for the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative, a U.S. defense program. 他们还敦促这两位官员拨出国会已经批准用于台湾购买武器的3亿美元援助，以及用于美国国防项目“台湾安全合作倡议”的10亿美元。 上周，美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔（左）与美国驻华大使庞德伟在白宫合影。 Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times When a Fox News interviewer asked Mr. Perdue on Sunday about the widespread concerns over withheld weapons sales and military aid to Taiwan, Mr. Perdue pointed out that Mr. Trump had approved $11 billion of arms sales to Taiwan last year. And he said “there are continuing conversations about other sales. He and President Xi talk about that every time they get together.” 周日，当福克斯新闻的一位采访记者就外界对暂缓对台军售和军事援助的广泛担忧向庞德伟提问时，庞德伟指出，特朗普去年批准了对台110亿美元的军售。他说，“关于其他军售的对话仍在继续。他和习主席每次见面都会谈论这个问题。” It was then that Mr. Perdue said Mr. Trump had argued that the United States sells arms to “other people around the world,” and offered such sales to Mr. Xi. 就在这个时候，庞德伟说，特朗普曾主张美国向“世界各地的其他人”出售武器，并向习近平提出了此类军售提议。 China has said Mr. Xi has told Mr. Trump that he opposes the United States selling weapons to Taiwan. In May, after leaving a Beijing summit with Mr. Xi, Mr. Trump told reporters he had discussed Taiwan arms sales with Mr. Xi “in great detail.” Such conversations — the existence of which Mr. Perdue underscored in his remarks on Sunday — are a violation of a 1982 document in which the United States agreed to broaden its support of Taiwan; one of the assurances said Washington “has not agreed to consult with” China on arms sales to Taiwan. 中国表示，习近平曾告诉特朗普，他反对美国向台湾出售武器。今年5月，在结束与习近平在北京举行的峰会后，特朗普告诉记者，他与习近平“非常详细地”讨论了对台军售问题。庞德伟在周日的采访中强调了这些对话的存在，而这些对话违反了1982年的一份文件，在该文件中，美国同意扩大对台湾的支持；其中一项保证指出，华盛顿“未同意”与中国就对台军售问题进行“磋商”。 When asked in May about that commitment, Mr. Trump replied: “Well, I think the 1980s is a long way. That’s a big, far distance.” 今年5月被问及该承诺时，特朗普回答说：“嗯，我认为1980年代是很久以前的事了。那是很远很远的距离。” In a Fox News interview recorded in May while he was in Beijing, Mr. Trump said he was holding back Taiwan arms sales because it was a “very good negotiating chip” with China. 在5月访问北京期间录制的福克斯新闻采访中，他表示，他之所以暂缓对台军售，是因为这是与中国谈判的“一张非常好的筹码”。 After the summit last week. Mr. Trump said he and Mr. Xi did not talk much about Taiwan. “Right now, it’s fine,” he said. “It’s just moving along.” 在上周的峰会之后。特朗普表示他和习近平没有太多谈论台湾。“现在情况还不错，”他说。“一切正在向前发展。” On Sunday, Taiwan’s de facto ambassador to the United States, Alexander Yui, said on CBS News’s “Face the Nation” that he felt confident, based on public remarks last week by administration officials, that “there’s no change in Taiwan’s position for the United States.” He added, though, that he hoped Taiwan could get the $14 billion withheld arms package “as soon as possible.” 周日，台湾事实上的驻美大使俞大㵢在CBS新闻的《面向全国》节目中表示，基于美国政府官员上周的公开讲话，他感到很有信心，“美国对台湾的立场没有改变”。不过他还说，他希望台湾能“尽快”获得被搁置的140亿美元武器方案。 On Wednesday, Mr. Rubio was asked by reporters in New York about the withholding of the Taiwan arms package. He said the sale was being reviewed in light of the need for “balancing our industrial capacity and our military-industrial base” and determining whether the United States needed the arms for itself. It is unclear how Mr. Trump’s offer to sell arms to China is consistent with that reasoning. 周三，鲁比奥在纽约被记者问及暂缓对台军售一事。他说，考虑到需要“平衡我们的工业能力和军工基地”，并确定美国自身是否需要这些武器，该军售正在接受审查。目前尚不清楚特朗普提出向中国出售武器的提议如何与这一理由保持相符。 Mr. Trump said last week that he would meet with Mr. Xi again in China in November during a regional leadership summit, and that the Chinese leader would return to the United States in December, also for a multilateral summit. Analysts say it is unlikely that Mr. Trump will approve any sales of arms to Taiwan before the end of the year, for fear of upsetting Mr. Xi before those planned meetings. 特朗普上周表示，他将于11月在中国举行的区域领导人峰会上再次与习近平会晤，后者也将于12月重返美国，参加一场多边峰会。分析人士表示，特朗普不太可能在年底前批准对台任何军售，以免在这些计划中的会晤之前惹恼习近平。 黄安伟(Edward Wong)为《纽约时报》报道全球事务、美国外交政策和国务院新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
content: 黄安伟 2026年9月28日 中国国家主席习近平上周对美国进行国事访问。中国是全球军事力量增长最快的国家。 Kenny Holston/The New York Times President Trump has asked Xi Jinping, the leader of China, whether he would like to buy American weapons, David Perdue, the American ambassador to China, said in a television interview on Sunday. 美国驻华大使庞德伟(David Perdue)在周日的电视采访中表示，特朗普总统曾询问中国领导人习近平是否愿意购买美国武器。 “President Trump continues to say, ‘Hey, we sell arms to other people around the world,’” Mr. Perdue said on “Fox News Sunday” while discussing the state visit by Mr. Xi to Washington last week. “He actually asked President Xi would he like to buy some at one point.” “特朗普总统一直说，‘嘿，我们向世界各地的其他人出售武器。’他实际上问过习主席，是否愿意买一些，”庞德伟 在《福克斯周日新闻》上讨论 习近平上周对华盛顿的 国事访问 时说。 Mr. Perdue did not give further details and did not reveal Mr. Xi’s reply. 庞德伟没有提供更多细节，也没有透露习近平的答复。 An admission that the American president offered to sell arms to China is extraordinary. The Communist-ruled nation is considered by most American policymakers and legislators of both parties to be the greatest military, economic and diplomatic rival of the United States — the only real challenger to America as a superpower. 承认美国总统曾提出向中国出售武器，这是极不寻常的。这个由共产党执政的国家被美国两党大多数政策制定者和立法者视为美国在军事、经济和外交上的最大对手——也是美国作为超级大国的唯一真正挑战者。 When asked for comment, the White House said through a U.S. official that the United States had no plans to sell arms to China. The State Department said in a statement that “U.S. law prohibits arms sales to China and there is no offer or plan to sell arms to China.” 在被要求置评时，白宫通过一名美国官员表示，美国没有向中国出售武器的计划。美国国务院在声明中表示，“美国法律禁止向中国出售武器，并且没有向中国出售武器的提议或计划。” The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment. 中国驻华盛顿大使馆没有立即回应置评请求。 China has the world’s fastest-growing military, and for decades U.S. officials across administrations, including in the current one, have warned of a potential military clash between the two nuclear-armed powers in the Asia-Pacific region, particularly over the island of Taiwan or China’s aggressive actions in territory claimed by U.S. allies in the South and East China Seas. 中国拥有世界上发展最快的军队，几十年来，包括现任政府在内的历届美国政府官员都曾警告，这两个核武大国之间在亚太地区 可能发生军事冲突 ，特别是围绕台湾问题，或是由于中国在美国盟友声称拥有主权的南海和东海领土采取的 强硬行动 。 Chinese defense companies, with the approval of the Chinese government, are supporting adversaries of the United States, including Iran and Russia , by selling them dual-use equipment and satellite imagery , as well as planning the secret export of weapons, according to U.S. officials. The United States has imposed sanctions on some Chinese companies. 据美国官员称，在得到中国政府批准的情况下，中国国防企业正在通过出售军民两用设备和 卫星图像 ，以及 策划秘密出口 武器，来 支持 包括 伊朗 和 俄罗斯 在内的美国对手。美国已经对部分中国企业实施了制裁。 The United States has been the dominant military power in the Asia-Pacific region, but that strength is fading relative to China’s, especially as the Trump administration diverts resources from the region for use in its war against Iran . In recent years, the U.S. defense industry has also struggled to manufacture weapons systems at a rate considered sufficient for global needs by American officials. 美国一直是亚太地区的主导军事力量，但相对于中国，这种力量正在衰退，尤其是随着特朗普政府将该地区的资源调往 对伊朗的战争 中。近年来，美国国防工业也一直难以按照美国官员认为能满足全球需求的速度来制造武器系统。 “If there was any ambiguity about whether President Trump views China as a security threat, this disclosure by @USAmbChina Perdue puts the question to rest,” Ryan Hass, a former career diplomat and White House national security official who is director of the China center at the Brookings Institution, wrote on social media . “如果说对于特朗普总统是否将中国视为安全威胁还存在含糊之处，那么@USAmbChina（美国驻华大使）庞德伟的这一披露让这个问题有了定论，”前职业外交官、白宫国家安全官员、布鲁金斯学会中国中心主任何瑞恩(Ryan Hass) 在社交媒体上写道 。 “Trump’s offer to sell weapons to China will be unsettling to American partners at the pointy edge of China’s spear,” he added. “特朗普向中国出售武器的提议将让处于中国矛头最前沿的美国合作伙伴感到不安，”他还说。 Those partners include the Philippines, Japan and Taiwan, the de facto independent island and democracy that the Chinese Communist Party seeks to rule . 这些合作伙伴包括菲律宾、日本和台湾，台湾是一个事实上的独立岛屿和民主政体，是中国共产党 企图统治 的对象。 Mr. Trump has been withholding a $14 billion sale of weapons to Taiwan, even though the U.S. government has been required by law since 1979 to send arms of a defensive nature to the island. The latest arms package was put together by State Department officials and was approved by congressional leaders early this year, but has since languished at the department, The New York Times reported . 特朗普一直搁置向台湾出售价值140亿美元的武器，尽管自1979年以来，美国政府 在法律上被要求 向该岛提供防御性武器。据《纽约时报》 报道 ，最新的军售一揽子计划由国务院官员拟定，并在今年早些时候获得了国会领导人的批准，但此后便一直被搁置在国务院。 Senators sent a bipartisan letter in May to Mr. Trump urging him to move forward with the sales. On Wednesday, hours before Mr. Xi arrived in Washington, four Republican senators led by Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asking for the same thing. 今年5月，参议员们向特朗普发送了一封 两党联名信 ，敦促他推进军售。周三，就在习近平抵达华盛顿前几个小时，由肯塔基州参议员米奇·麦康奈尔牵头的四位共和党参议员 致信 国务卿马可·鲁比奥和国防部长皮特·海格塞斯，提出了同样的要求。 They also pressed the two men to allocate $300 million in aid for purchasing arms that Congress had already approved for Taiwan, as well as $1 billion for the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative, a U.S. defense program. 他们还敦促这两位官员拨出国会已经批准用于台湾购买武器的3亿美元援助，以及用于美国国防项目“台湾安全合作倡议”的10亿美元。 上周，美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔（左）与美国驻华大使庞德伟在白宫合影。 Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times When a Fox News interviewer asked Mr. Perdue on Sunday about the widespread concerns over withheld weapons sales and military aid to Taiwan, Mr. Perdue pointed out that Mr. Trump had approved $11 billion of arms sales to Taiwan last year. And he said “there are continuing conversations about other sales. He and President Xi talk about that every time they get together.” 周日，当福克斯新闻的一位采访记者就外界对暂缓对台军售和军事援助的广泛担忧向庞德伟提问时，庞德伟指出，特朗普去年批准了对台110亿美元的军售。他说，“关于其他军售的对话仍在继续。他和习主席每次见面都会谈论这个问题。” It was then that Mr. Perdue said Mr. Trump had argued that the United States sells arms to “other people around the world,” and offered such sales to Mr. Xi. 就在这个时候，庞德伟说，特朗普曾主张美国向“世界各地的其他人”出售武器，并向习近平提出了此类军售提议。 China has said Mr. Xi has told Mr. Trump that he opposes the United States selling weapons to Taiwan. In May, after leaving a Beijing summit with Mr. Xi, Mr. Trump told reporters he had discussed Taiwan arms sales with Mr. Xi “in great detail.” Such conversations — the existence of which Mr. Perdue underscored in his remarks on Sunday — are a violation of a 1982 document in which the United States agreed to broaden its support of Taiwan; one of the assurances said Washington “has not agreed to consult with” China on arms sales to Taiwan. 中国表示，习近平曾告诉特朗普，他反对美国向台湾出售武器。今年5月，在结束与习近平在北京举行的峰会后，特朗普告诉记者，他与习近平“非常详细地”讨论了对台军售问题。庞德伟在周日的采访中强调了这些对话的存在，而这些对话违反了1982年的一份文件，在该文件中，美国同意扩大对台湾的支持； 其中一项保证指出，华盛顿 “未同意”与中国就对台军售问题进行“磋商”。 When asked in May about that commitment, Mr. Trump replied: “Well, I think the 1980s is a long way. That’s a big, far distance.” 今年5月被问及该承诺时，特朗普回答说：“嗯，我认为1980年代是很久以前的事了。那是很远很远的距离。” In a Fox News interview recorded in May while he was in Beijing, Mr. Trump said he was holding back Taiwan arms sales because it was a “very good negotiating chip” with China. 在5月访问北京期间录制的福克斯新闻采访中，他表示，他之所以暂缓对台军售，是因为这是与中国谈判的“一张非常好的筹码”。 After the summit last week. Mr. Trump said he and Mr. Xi did not talk much about Taiwan. “Right now, it’s fine,” he said. “It’s just moving along.” 在上周的峰会之后。特朗普表示他和习近平没有太多谈论台湾。“现在情况还不错，”他说。“一切正在向前发展。” On Sunday, Taiwan’s de facto ambassador to the United States, Alexander Yui, said on CBS News’s “Face the Nation” that he felt confident, based on public remarks last week by administration officials, that “there’s no change in Taiwan’s position for the United States.” He added, though, that he hoped Taiwan could get the $14 billion withheld arms package “as soon as possible.” 周日，台湾事实上的驻美大使俞大㵢在 CBS新闻的《面向全国》节目 中表示，基于美国政府官员上周的公开讲话，他感到很有信心，“美国对台湾的立场没有改变”。不过他还说，他希望台湾能“尽快”获得被搁置的140亿美元武器方案。 On Wednesday, Mr. Rubio was asked by reporters in New York about the withholding of the Taiwan arms package. He said the sale was being reviewed in light of the need for “balancing our industrial capacity and our military-industrial base” and determining whether the United States needed the arms for itself. It is unclear how Mr. Trump’s offer to sell arms to China is consistent with that reasoning. 周三，鲁比奥在纽约被记者问及暂缓对台军售一事。他说，考虑到需要“平衡我们的工业能力和军工基地”，并确定美国自身是否需要这些武器，该军售正在接受审查。目前尚不清楚特朗普提出向中国出售武器的提议如何与这一理由保持相符。 Mr. Trump said last week that he would meet with Mr. Xi again in China in November during a regional leadership summit, and that the Chinese leader would return to the United States in December, also for a multilateral summit. Analysts say it is unlikely that Mr. Trump will approve any sales of arms to Taiwan before the end of the year, for fear of upsetting Mr. Xi before those planned meetings. 特朗普上周表示，他将于11月在中国举行的区域领导人峰会上再次与习近平会晤，后者也将于12月重返美国，参加一场多边峰会。分析人士表示，特朗普不太可能在年底前批准对台任何军售，以免在这些计划中的会晤之前惹恼习近平。 黄安伟( Edward Wong )为《纽约时报》报道全球事务、美国外交政策和国务院新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 从台海到日本，习近平试图“撬动”特朗普的亚太立场
description: 储百亮, DAVID PIERSON2026年9月28日中国领导人习近平和特朗普总统周四在白宫举行的欢迎仪式上。 Doug Mills/The New York Times China’s leader, Xi Jinping, is not known for lightheartedness. Yet during his White House summit with President Trump, he sometimes smiled and even laughed, projecting a warmth unusual for a meeting between superpower rivals. 中国领导人习近平素来不以轻松诙谐著称。但在与特朗普总统的白宫峰会上，他时而微笑，时而甚至开怀大笑，展现出超级大国对手间的会晤中并不常见的暖意。 Behind the show of geniality, Mr. Xi’s carefully chosen words revealed a cooler calculus: an effort to steer Mr. Trump toward Beijing’s positions on Taiwan, Japan and the broader security order in Asia. 在亲切表象的背后，习近平精心选择的措辞透露出更为冷静的盘算：试图将特朗普引向北京在台湾、日本以及更广泛的亚洲安全秩序问题上的立场。 On Taiwan, Mr. Xi pressed Mr. Trump to limit American support for the self-ruled island that Beijing claims as its territory. On Japan, Mr. Xi invoked history to portray Tokyo, an American ally, as a resurgent military threat, while reminding the president that China and the United States had once fought on the same side. 在台湾问题上，习近平向特朗普施压，要求限制美国对这个北京声称拥有主权的自治岛屿的支持。在日本问题上，他援引历史，将美国的盟友东京描绘成一个重新崛起的军事威胁，同时提醒特朗普，中美两国曾经并肩作战。 Mr. Xi appeared to be testing for opportunities to shape Mr. Trump’s views, rather than hoping for a decisive breakthrough, Matt Pottinger, who served as a deputy national security adviser to Mr. Trump in his first term as president, said in an interview. Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump have met three times since October last year, and they may meet two more times by the end of this year. 曾在特朗普首个总统任期内担任副国家安全顾问的博明(Matt Pottinger)在接受采访时表示,习近平似乎是在试探是否有机会影响特朗普的看法，而不是期待取得决定性突破。自去年10月以来，习近平和特朗普已会面三次，年底前可能还会再见两次。 “Xi sees frequent meetings with his American counterpart as an opportunity to probe for weaknesses in the U.S. positions,” said Mr. Pottinger, now the chairman of the China Program at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies. 现任捍卫民主基金会中国项目主席的博明说：“习近平把与美国总统频繁会晤视为一个机会，可以借此试探美国立场中的薄弱之处。” Outwardly, the summit between Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump achieved little. 从表面上看，习近平与特朗普的此次峰会成果寥寥。 China and the United States agreed to extend their truce in the trade war, but only by two months. The leaders discussed the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine but announced no apparent advances on ending either conflict. They toasted each other, and spoke loftily of partnership and stability in relations, yet announced no concrete agreements on the most contentious of issues: the trade imbalance, technology restrictions and Taiwan. 中美双方同意延长贸易战休战期，但仅延长两个月。两位领导人讨论了中东和乌克兰的战争，但并未宣布在结束其中任何一场冲突方面取得明显进展。他们彼此举杯致意，高谈伙伴关系和双边关系的稳定，但在最棘手的几个问题——贸易失衡、技术限制和台湾——上，没有宣布任何具体协议。 周四在白宫举行的国宴上互致祝酒词时，两位领导人都高谈美中伙伴关系和双边关系的稳定。 The White House did announce that it had reached a deal with China to reduce tariffs on $30 billion of “nonsensitive goods.” The two nations also agreed to continue to discuss supply-chain issues with critical minerals, as well as concerns over artificial intelligence. But the White House did not detail specific plans on those more contentious points. 白宫确实宣布，已与中国达成协议，将降低对300亿美元“非敏感商品”的关税。两国还同意继续就关键矿产的供应链问题以及人工智能方面的担忧进行讨论。但白宫没有就这些更具争议的问题公布体计划。 The trip was certainly a propaganda boost for Mr. Xi, who has sought to cast himself as an equal to Mr. Trump on the world stage. 这次访问无疑对习近平来说是一次宣传上的助力。长期以来，他一直试图把自己塑造成在世界舞台上与特朗普平起平坐的领导人。 Coverage of the summit was splashed across the front page of the People’s Daily, the Communist Party’s mouthpiece, with images of Mr. Xi being honored at the White House with a military flyover and being greeted by Mr. Trump at Joint Base Andrews. A top trending hashtag on Chinese social media was about how rare it was for an American president to receive a world leader on the tarmac. 中共机关报《人民日报》在头版大篇幅报道了这次峰会，并刊登了习近平在白宫接受军机飞行致敬、在安德鲁斯空军基地受到特朗普迎接的照片。中国社交媒体上的一个热门话题是，美国总统机场迎接外国领导人多么罕见。 “This is historic validation of China’s strength. It’s seen as a point of arrival and adds to Xi Jinping’s effort to portray China as an equal partner, which has been the brass ring of Chinese foreign policy” for decades, said Evan Medeiros, a professor of Asian studies at Georgetown University who was senior Asia director on the National Security Council under President Barack Obama. 乔治敦大学亚洲研究教授、奥巴马总统任内曾任国家安全委员会亚洲事务高级主任的麦艾文(Evan Medeiros)说：“这是对中国实力具有历史意义的认可。人们把它视为一个抵达目标的时刻，也为习近平把中国塑造成平等伙伴的努力增添了分量——几十年来，这一直是中国外交政策梦寐以求的目标。” The summit served Mr. Xi’s purposes in a more subtle but important way. He used verbal finesse to suggest that Mr. Trump was sympathetic to Beijing’s positions — even if members of Mr. Trump’s own administration disagree with them. 这场峰会还以一种更为微妙却同样重要的方式契合了习近平的目的。他运用言辞上的巧妙分寸暗示特朗普对北京的立场抱有同情，即使特朗普政府内部的一些成员实际上并不认同这些立场。 Most notably, Mr. Xi appeared to imply that Mr. Trump had shifted closer to Beijing’s views on Taiwan, including that the island’s government is scheming for independence. Continued stability in relations between China and the United States, he indicated, rested on Mr. Trump heeding Chinese positions. 最值得注意的是，习近平似乎在暗示，特朗普在台湾问题上的立场已经更接近北京，包括认同台湾当局正在谋求独立这一说法。他还暗示，中美关系能否继续保持稳定，取决于特朗普是否听取中方立场。 “I hope that the United States adheres to the correct position of opposing ‘Taiwan independence’ and handles the Taiwan issue prudently,” Mr. Xi said in his meeting with Mr. Trump on Thursday, according to an official summary issued by Chinese news outlets. That approach would, Mr. Xi said, “lay a solid foundation for U.S.-China strategic cooperation and the development of bilateral relations.” 据中国官方通稿，习近平周四与特朗普的会晤中表示：“希望美方坚持反对‘台独’的正确立场，慎重处理台湾问题。”习近平说，这种做法将“为中美战略合作和两国关系发展奠定坚实基础”。 台湾台北的一座自由女神像复制品。习近平告诉特朗普，“希望美方坚持反对‘台独’的正确立场。” Successive U.S. administrations have said they do not support outright Taiwanese independence. But U.S. presidents have generally rejected Chinese calls for Washington to declare that it flatly “opposes” independence. Such a shift, experts say, could suggest that the United States believes that Taiwan’s policies, and not Beijing’s threat of forcible unification, are the primary source of cross-strait tensions. 历届美国政府都表示不支持台湾正式宣布独立。但美国总统通常拒绝接受中方要求华盛顿明确宣布“反对”台湾独立的主张。多位专家指出，如果美国作出这样的转变，可能意味着华盛顿认为，两岸紧张局势的主要根源在于台湾自身的政策，而非北京方面的武统威胁。 Mr. Xi’s use of the word “adhere” (“jianchi” in Chinese) appeared intended to create the impression that “Beijing believes Trump has already absorbed some of its red lines on Taiwan,” said Craig Singleton, a China Program senior director at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies. “Beijing is steadily wrapping its preferred language around the summit.” 捍卫民主基金会中国项目高级主任克雷格·辛格顿说，习近平使用“坚持”一词，似乎是为了营造这样一种印象：“北京认为，特朗普已经接受了中方在台湾问题上划定的红线。”他说：“北京正在稳步地把自己偏好的措辞套在这次峰会上。” The official Chinese summary of Mr. Xi’s remarks did not go into specifics, but the implied warning was clear, several experts said. If Mr. Trump went ahead and approved a proposal to sell $14 billion worth of weapons to Taiwan, he could damage or even undo the fragile détente between Beijing and Washington. 中方发布的这份官方通稿并未就习近平的表态展开具体阐述，但多位专家指出，其中隐含的警告意味已相当明显。倘若特朗普执意批准一项价值140亿美元的对台军售提案，就可能损害、甚至彻底破坏北京和华盛顿之间脆弱的缓和关系。 The package includes missiles, anti-drone equipment and air-defense systems. It would follow a separate $11 billion package Mr. Trump approved late last year. After his last summit with Mr. Xi in Beijing in May, though, Mr. Trump said that the arms sales were a “very good negotiating chip” with China. He has since held off on approving the new package, raising unease in Taiwan and across Asia about how far he could go in subordinating U.S. security commitments to better ties with China. 这批军售包括导弹、反无人机设备和防空系统。此前，特朗普已于去年年底批准另一批价值110亿美元的对台军售。不过，今年5月在北京与习近平举行上一次峰会后，特朗普说，对台军售是与中国谈判时“一张非常好的筹码”。此后，他一直没有批准这批新的军售，这也在台湾以及整个亚洲地区引发了不安，人们担心他可能在多大程度上为了改善对华关系而把美国的安全承诺置于次要位置。 “What is important is in practice the U.S. should stop selling arms to Taiwan and be very careful in the dealing with Taiwan,” said Wu Xinbo, an American studies scholar at Fudan University in Shanghai who advises China’s Foreign Ministry. “重要的是，在实践中，美国应停止向台湾出售武器，并在非常谨慎地处理台湾问题，”上海复旦大学美国研究学者、为中国外交部提供咨询的吴心伯说。 Many experts expect Mr. Trump to eventually sign off on more arms sales, however. China could retaliate with military intimidation of Taiwan or economic punishment of the United States, such as further restrictions of rare earth exports to U.S. companies. 不过，许多专家预计，特朗普最终仍会批准更多对台军售。中国可能通过对台湾进行军事恫吓或者对美国实施经济惩罚来报复，例如进一步限制向美国企业出口稀土。 Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Mr. Xi’s comments “distorted the facts” in an effort to support Beijing’s claim over the island. 台湾外交部表示，习近平的言论“扭曲事实”，目的是为北京对台湾的主权主张提供支持。 今年8月，台湾陆军在彰化举行的“汉光”军事演习中操作无人机。 Ali Wyne, a senior researcher on U.S.-China ties at the International Crisis Group, said Mr. Xi recognizes that Mr. Trump was “not going to dwell on semantic considerations, especially if he can frame them as part of an appeal to Trump’s ego.” 国际危机组织的美中关系高级研究员阿里·韦恩说，习近平意识到，特朗普“不会纠结于语义上的考量，尤其是如果他能把这些措辞包装成一种迎合特朗普自尊的说法”。 For that, Mr. Xi leaned into a familiar maritime metaphor that appealed to Mr. Trump’s preference for leader-to-leader diplomacy. “I am ready to work with you to steer the giant ship of the China-U.S. relationship on a steady course,” Mr. Xi told Mr. Trump. 为此，习近平再次使用了一个熟悉的航海比喻，迎合特朗普偏好领导人之间直接外交的风格。习近平对特朗普说：“我们应当共同扛起这个历史重任，推动中美关系这艘巨轮沿着正确航道平稳前行。” Mr. Trump said on Friday that he would attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, in November, and that Mr. Xi would attend the Group of 20 summit in Florida in December. 特朗普周五表示，他将出席11月在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织峰会，而习近平将出席12月在佛罗里达举行的二十国集团峰会。 Mr. Xi also used his time to try to drive a wedge between Washington and one of its stalwart allies in Asia — Japan. 习近平还利用这次会晤，试图在华盛顿与日本之间制造裂痕，日本是美国在亚洲最坚定的盟友之一。 He reminded Mr. Trump that the United States and China fought together against a common Japanese enemy during World War II. content: 储百亮, DAVID PIERSON 2026年9月28日 中国领导人习近平和特朗普总统周四在白宫举行的欢迎仪式上。 Doug Mills/The New York Times China’s leader, Xi Jinping, is not known for lightheartedness. Yet during his White House summit with President Trump, he sometimes smiled and even laughed, projecting a warmth unusual for a meeting between superpower rivals. 中国领导人习近平素来不以轻松诙谐著称。但在与特朗普总统的白宫峰会上，他时而微笑，时而甚至开怀大笑，展现出超级大国对手间的会晤中并不常见的暖意。 Behind the show of geniality, Mr. Xi’s carefully chosen words revealed a cooler calculus: an effort to steer Mr. Trump toward Beijing’s positions on Taiwan, Japan and the broader security order in Asia. 在亲切表象的背后，习近平精心选择的措辞透露出更为冷静的盘算：试图将特朗普引向北京在台湾、日本以及更广泛的亚洲安全秩序问题上的立场。 On Taiwan, Mr. Xi pressed Mr. Trump to limit American support for the self-ruled island that Beijing claims as its territory. On Japan, Mr. Xi invoked history to portray Tokyo, an American ally, as a resurgent military threat, while reminding the president that China and the United States had once fought on the same side. 在台湾问题上，习近平向特朗普施压，要求限制美国对这个北京声称拥有主权的自治岛屿的支持。在日本问题上，他援引历史，将美国的盟友东京描绘成一个重新崛起的军事威胁，同时提醒特朗普，中美两国曾经并肩作战。 Mr. Xi appeared to be testing for opportunities to shape Mr. Trump’s views, rather than hoping for a decisive breakthrough, Matt Pottinger, who served as a deputy national security adviser to Mr. Trump in his first term as president, said in an interview. He described Imperial Japan as “fascist” and “militarist” aggressors, reviving an image of Japan as an “ enemy state ” that cannot be trusted on the global stage. 他提醒特朗普，第二次世界大战期间，美中曾共同抗击日本这个共同敌人。他把日本帝国称为“法西斯”和“军国主义”侵略者，重新唤起一种把日本描绘成全球舞台上不值得信任的“ 敌国 ”的形象。 His remarks were in line with a monthslong effort by Beijing to punish Japan over comments Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi made in defense of Taiwan in November. 他的这些言论与北京几个月来针对日本展开的施压行动一脉相承。去年11月，日本首相高市早苗发表了支持台湾的言论，此后北京一直试图让日本为此付出代价。 日本首相高市早苗今年3月在白宫。习近平在与特朗普会晤时试图在美日之间制造裂痕。 “The message is, ‘They are the bad guys, and we are the good guys that are trying to change the world order, and the Americans should cooperate with us,’” said Akio Takahara, a visiting professor at Tokyo Woman’s Christian University who specializes in Chinese politics. 专攻中国政治的东京女子大学客座教授高原明生说：“传递的信息是：‘他们是坏人，而我们才是试图改变世界秩序的好人，美国人应该与我们合作。’” The risk for Japan, he said, is that Mr. Xi’s narrative could gain traction if repeated enough times. 他说，对日本而言，风险在于，如果习近平不断重复这种叙事，可能会获得越来越多的认同。 Ms. Takaichi told reporters in Tokyo on Friday that Japan had achieved “genuine reconciliation” with the United States and they now had a “relationship of mutual trust as allies bound by very strong bonds.” 高市早苗周五在东京对记者说，日本已经与美国实现了“真正的和解”，如今是“以非常牢固的纽带相连、彼此信赖的盟友关系”。 赫海威(Javier C. Hernández)自东京、Xinyun Wu自台北、Zolan Kanno-Youngs自华盛顿对本文有报道贡献。 储百亮( Chris Buckley )是《纽约时报》首席中国记者，自台北报道中国和台湾问题，重点关注政治、社会变革以及安全和军事问题。 David Pierson 报道中国外交政策和中国与世界的经济与文化交互。他从事新闻工作已超过20年。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

title: 在国宴上穿裤子的美国第一夫人
description: VANESSA FRIEDMAN2026年9月26日周四，在白宫举行的国宴前，特朗普总统、梅拉尼娅·特朗普、习近平主席及夫人彭丽媛合影留念。 Doug Mills/The New York Times Well, that was a surprise. 这可真是出人意料。 In what may have been a first for an American first lady, Melania Trump did something at the state dinner for China’s leader on Thursday night that none of her predecessors had likely done before: She wore pants. 在周四晚为中国领导人举行的国宴上，梅拉尼娅·特朗普做了一件可能是美国第一夫人史上前所未有、她的各位前任大概都没做过的事：她穿了裤子。 Pants! To a black-tie banquet. Especially a black-tie banquet taking place at a highly sensitive time in global geopolitics and economic relations. 裤子！还是穿去参加正装晚宴。更何况，这场正装晚宴正值全球地缘政治和经济关系极为敏感的时期。 Specifically, Mrs. Trump wore a pair of peony-print Dolce & Gabbana black tuxedo pants with a white Saint Laurent blouse displaying an enormous bow to join her husband in welcoming the Chinese president, Xi Jinping; his wife, Peng Liyuan; and assorted dignitaries (including many tech executives) to the formal occasion. 具体来说，特朗普夫人穿了一条印有牡丹图案的杜嘉班纳黑色礼服长裤，搭配一件带有巨大蝴蝶结的圣罗兰白色衬衫。她与丈夫一起出席这个正式场合，迎接中国国家主席习近平、其夫人彭丽媛以及各界要人（包括许多科技高管）。 The peony print on the pants may have been a nod to that flower’s importance in Chinese culture, where it is a symbol of beauty, wealth and happiness. In the end though, that subtle gesture was less significant than the norm-busting choice of the pants themselves on an occasion that has traditionally been synonymous with elaborate gowns. Or at least evening skirts. 裤装上的牡丹图案或许是在致意这种花在中国文化中的重要地位，在中国，它是美丽、财富和幸福的象征。不过，在这样一个传统上与华丽礼服（或至少是晚礼服裙）画等号的场合，这种微妙的致敬远不如选择长裤这一打破常规的举动本身更有意义。 Pants for evening is no longer a radical idea in most situations, but in a city that has become the last bastion of the suit and tie, where staid rules about fashion and the clothing that is fit for office still apply, they were a statement. 在大多数情况下，晚宴穿裤装已不再是一个激进的想法，但在这个已成为西装领结最后堡垒的城市，在有关时尚和职场着装的古板规则依然适用的地方，这个选择就成为一种宣言。 Especially in contrast with the more classic dress of Ms. Peng — a long gown with a Mandarin collar in red, China’s color of prosperity — as well as Mr. Trump’s tuxedo and Mr. Xi’s Zhongshan suit, standard choices both. (Not to mention the apparently matching navy suits and magenta ties they wore during their meeting earlier in the day.) 特别是，这与彭丽媛更为经典的着装形成鲜明对比——彭丽媛身穿中式立领红色长礼服，红色在中国象征着繁荣——还有特朗普的无尾礼服和习近平的中山装，两者都是标准的选择）。（更不用说他们两人在当天早些时候会面时所穿、看似很搭配的海军蓝西装和洋红色领带。） 梅拉尼娅·特朗普身着杜嘉班纳长裤和圣罗兰衬衫，与身着经典红色礼服的彭丽媛一同步入国宴现场。 When it comes to Melania Trump, however, the pants were also entirely on brand. They reflected the first lady’s continued reluctance to conform to archetypal expectations for first spouses. 然而，就梅拉尼娅·特朗普而言，裤装也完全符合她的个人风格。这反映出这位第一夫人一如既往地不愿顺从人们对第一配偶这一角色的刻板期待。 And they underscored once again the individual brand Mrs. Trump has been building since the release of her documentary earlier this year, with its focus on slick black-and-white graphics and luxury labels, on-screen as in her wardrobe. (That they also matched the pandas Mr. Xi offered to the Atlanta zoo as “envoys of friendship” was probably a coincidence.) 这也再次凸显了特朗普夫人自今年早些时候她的纪录片发布以来一直在打造的个人品牌形象，无论是银幕上还是她的衣橱里，都以精致的黑白图形和奢侈品牌为特色。（至于这样的打扮刚好与习近平作为“友谊的使者”赠送给亚特兰大动物园的大熊猫相呼应，大概只是个巧合。） Indeed, a Dolce & Gabbana pantsuit has become a uniform of sorts for the first lady since her husband returned to office. She wore Dolce for her official portrait in 2025 (the one that made her look like chairman of the board), to the White House dinner with governors the same year and to the State of the Union address earlier this year. 事实上，自从她丈夫重返白宫以来，杜嘉班纳的裤装已经成为这位第一夫人的某种制服。她在2025年拍摄官方肖像时（那张让她看起来像董事会主席的照片）、在同年各州州长出席的白宫晚宴上，以及在今年早些时候的国情咨文演讲中，穿的都是杜嘉班纳。 The look suggests that she views her role less like that of the hostess of the nation and more like that of an executive in a giant corporation. The buttoned-up styles also guard against the intrusive eyes and demands of the watching world and the country the first family represents. 这种造型表明，她将自己的角色更多地视为一家巨型企业的高管，而非国家的女主人。这种严谨的风格也帮她抵御外界窥探的目光与种种要求——这一切既来自注视着她的世界，也来自第一家庭所代表的国家。 周四，第一夫人身着亚历山大·麦昆套装。周三，第一夫人身着纪梵希细条纹西装，在安德鲁斯联合基地迎接彭丽媛。 You could see it with the giant bow on the blouse Mrs. Trump wore to the state dinner, which jutted out like a shield from the shirt’s equally protective high neck. You could see it in the military-style charcoal Alexander McQueen skirt suit she wore earlier in the day to tour the Smithsonian alongside Ms. Peng, with the jacket’s officer collar and side closure. And you could see it in the Givenchy pinstriped suit she wore to accompany her husband to Joint Base Andrews for the arrival of the Chinese leader. 从特朗普夫人国宴所穿衬衫上的巨大蝴蝶结可以看出这一点，它像盾牌一样，从同样具有保护性的衬衫高领处突出。你可以从她当天早些时候陪同彭丽媛参观史密森尼学会时穿的军装风炭灰色亚历山大·麦昆裙装中看出这一点，那件外套带有军官领和侧边纽扣。你还可以从她陪同丈夫前往安德鲁斯联合基地迎接中国领导人到来时穿的纪梵希细条纹套装中看出这一点。 That’s why, though it would be nice to interpret Mrs. Trump’s choice of pants as a win for women’s liberation everywhere (really, it is ridiculous that it took until 2026 for a first lady to wear pants to a state dinner), it seems unlikely that the motivating factor was gender advancement. Rather than, say, personal priorities. 正因如此，尽管将特朗普夫人选择裤装解读为全球女性解放的胜利，这样的说法听起来很美好（说真的，直到2026年才有一位第一夫人穿裤装出席国宴，这太荒唐了），但其背后的动机似乎不太可能是为了推动性别进步，倒不如说是出于个人事项的优先考量。 Vanessa Friedman自2014年以来一直担任时报时尚总监和首席时尚评论家。

title: 白宫国宴：AI巨头与习近平共进晚餐，特朗普脱稿演讲
description: SHAWN McCREESH2026年9月26日周四晚，特朗普总统和中国国家主席习近平携夫人出席了在白宫举行的国宴。 Doug Mills/The New York Times It was just a fun little dinner for the people deciding the future of humanity. 这不过是为决定人类未来者举办的一场轻松愉快的小型晚宴。 The amount of power concentrated at the head table alone was dizzying. The American president and the Chinese president, dining by candlelight with Elon Musk, Jensen Huang and Tim Cook, all of them sitting in the State Dining room of the White House at this moment that many in Silicon Valley warn could be the last before mankind stumbles into the A.I. apocalypse. 光是主桌上汇聚的权力就令人目眩。美国总统和中国国家主席与埃隆·马斯克、黄仁勋和蒂姆·库克在烛光下共进晚餐。此刻，他们全都坐在白宫的国宴厅里，而硅谷的许多人警告说，这可能是人类陷入人工智能末日之前的最后时刻。 周四晚上的国宴场面极为隆重。 Standing before a room chockablock with A.I. moguls, billionaires and politicians, President Trump decided to depart from his prepared remarks. Now that he finally had these people together in one place, he could talk about his important plans. The ones he’s been working on nonstop ever since he returned to the White House. 站在挤满人工智能大亨、亿万富翁和政界人士的房间里，特朗普总统决定脱离准备好的讲稿。既然他终于把这些人聚在了一起，他就可以谈谈自己的重要计划——自从他重返白宫以来就一直不遗余力推进的计划。 “If I could go off-script, just for a second,” he said. “请允许我脱稿一下，就一小会儿，”他说。 The sound of rich people clapping filled the room. Suspense! 富人们热烈的掌声响彻全场。有悬念！ “I just want to say …” the president continued. “我只是想说……”总统继续道。 “… I’d like to invite everyone in the room to visit through that beautiful curtain in the back — The door, it’s all lit up, and looks beautiful. It’s one year away from completion, the new ballroom that you’ve heard about.” “……我想邀请在座各位穿过后面那道美丽的帷幕去参观——那扇门，亮着灯，看起来很漂亮。你们听说过的那个新宴会厅，距离完工还有一年的时间。” Oh. He was inviting them to take a walk through the construction site in back of the house. 哦。原来他是在邀请大家去白宫后面的建筑工地走走。 “You’ll be the first people to step foot on that,” he told guests including Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg and Sam Altman, “and we’ll do that maybe after we’re finished with the entertainment tonight.” “你们是第一批踏上那里的人，”他对包括杰夫·贝佐斯、马克·扎克伯格和萨姆·奥特曼在内的宾客们说，“也许等今晚的娱乐活动结束，我们就去那儿转转。” There was not a single mention of A.I. in his speech. Mr. Trump doesn’t buy into the A.I. panic. He insists it’s mostly just a problem of branding. A.I. needs better P.R. 在他的讲话中，根本没有提及人工智能。特朗普先生并不相信人工智能恐慌。他坚持认为这主要只是一个品牌包装问题。人工智能需要更好的公关。 If any of the tech titans and members of Chinese Politburo who showed up to the White House used the state visit to get on the same page about the direction of this terrifying new technology, they haven’t shared their designs with the public. This was a roomful of people who have many disagreements about the way forward. 就算出现在白宫的任何科技巨头和中国政治局委员利用这次国事访问，就这项可怕的新技术的发展方向达成了什么共识，他们也没有向公众透露他们的构想。这个房间里的人对于未来的发展方向存在诸多分歧。 在周四晚上的国宴上，特朗普邀请宾客参观新建宴会厅的施工现场。 The American president, for his part, just seemed happy to be playing maître d’ to the mighty. 就美国总统而言，他似乎只是乐于充当这些权贵们的领班角色。 “You will see something that I think you will really love,” Mr. Trump told them about the ballroom site. “Tonight, if we had it, we would have had way more than a thousand people, with standing room only. And this room has about 145, that’s about it.” “你们会看到一些我觉得你们会非常喜欢的东西，”特朗普在谈到宴会厅场地时对他们说。“今晚，如果我们有那个场地，到场人数肯定远远超过一千人，挤得水泄不通。而这个厅只能装145人左右，就这样了。” “Anybody who wants to walk into a construction site that’s nice and clean and sparkling, it’s our honor to have you do so,” he said. “This is in honor of President Xi, Madam Peng.” “任何想要走进一个整洁、干净、闪闪发光的建筑工地的人，我们都很荣幸能请你来参观，”他说。“这是为了向习近平主席和彭夫人致敬。” Mr. Trump never seems more pleased than when he is hosting wealthy and powerful people at his table. The aspects of the job that so clearly delight him concern pageantry and set design, and Mr. Xi’s visit provided opportunities for plenty of it. 特朗普最开心的时候似乎就是邀请富人和权贵坐在他的餐桌旁。这份工作中最能让他乐在其中的莫过于盛大的仪式和精心设计的场景，而习近平的访问为此提供了大量的机会。 Earlier in the day, Mr. Trump took Mr. Xi around the back to show off a new helipad and the slick new driveway. “He’s an expert on stone, aside from many others, and he loves good granite,” Mr. Trump told reporters as the pair walked back inside. 当天早些时候，特朗普带着习近平绕到后面，向他展示新建的直升机停机坪和光鲜的新车道。“他精通很多领域，还是石材专家，而且他特别喜欢上好的花岗岩，”两人走回室内时，特朗普对记者说。 特朗普带领习近平参观了新建的直升机停机坪。 Mr. Xi announced a gift of two giant pandas, named Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, who will live at the Atlanta zoo. At the dinner, Mr. Trump unveiled a rather large statue of a bald eagle to give to the Chinese autocrat. 习近平宣布赠送两只大熊猫作为礼物，它们名叫“平平”和“福双”，将会生活在亚特兰大动物园。在晚宴上，特朗普揭幕了一座相当大的白头海雕雕像，作为送给这位中国专制统治者的礼物。 “We hope it’ll find a nice place, a wonderful place, in Beijing,” Mr. Trump said. “我们希望它能在北京找到一个好地方，一个绝好的位置，”特朗普说。 Sadly for Mr. Trump, almost none of this made it onto the television networks he watches so closely. The Chinese state visit has collided with the consequences of the decision he made in a fit of pique last Friday to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House campus. A judge ordered the Trump administration to let the banned reporters back Thursday, but the TV networks are still refusing to take Mr. Trump’s carnival live. Until his administration formally agrees to let CNN back into the White House TV pool rotation, he is not going to see those blinking red lights he loves so much. 令特朗普遗憾的是，这一切几乎都没有出现在他密切关注的电视上。此次中国国家元首的访问恰好与他上周五一气之下做出的决定所带来的后果发生了冲突——他当时下令禁止CNN、MS NOW和Politico进入白宫区域。周四，一名法官下令特朗普政府允许被禁记者重返白宫，但各大电视网仍拒绝直播特朗普的这场嘉年华。除非他的政府正式同意让CNN重新加入白宫电视联合采访团轮换，否则他将无法看到那些他深深喜爱的闪烁红灯。 在国宴上，双方互赠了礼物，特朗普总统向这位中国领导人赠送了一尊白头海雕雕像。 Shortly before the dinner began, he posted one of his diatribes on his website. 就在晚宴开始前不久，他在自己的网站上发布了一篇抨击文章。 CNN and MS NOW were “fake,” he wrote, because they wouldn’t cover “one of the Biggest and Most Beautiful Events to take place in many years, the arrival at the White House of the Highly Respected President of China, Xi Jinping, and his beautiful wife, Madam Peng." 他写道，CNN和MS NOW是“假新闻”，因为它们拒绝报道“多年来最盛大、最美丽的活动之一——备受尊敬的中国国家主席习近平和他美丽的妻子彭夫人抵达白宫。” The president continued: “The event was magnificent — Actually made for Television but, because they’re Fake News, and because they knew how good it would be, they didn’t want credit to be given to ‘TRUMP,’ they refused to be there. That’s why they have such poor Ratings.” 总统还写道：“这场活动非常盛大——实际上就是为电视量身定做的，但因为它们是假新闻，而且因为它们知道这会有多棒，它们不想把功劳归于‘特朗普’，所以它们拒绝出席。所以它们的收视率才这么糟糕。” He concluded: “Tonight’s State Dinner at the White House, for President Xi, will be spectacular! The Media will be in attendance.” 他总结道：“今晚在白宫为习近平主席举行的国宴将会非常壮观！媒体届时也会到场。” Yes, the White House complex was crawling with journalists Thursday evening as Mr. Xi pulled up to the front door of the residence. But, in the spirit of solidarity with those targeted by Mr. Trump’s ban, some just ignored the spectacle. 是的，周四傍晚，当习近平抵达白宫官邸正门时，白宫建筑群内确实到处都是记者。但是，为了声援那些遭到特朗普禁令针对的人士，一些人对这个壮观的场面无动于衷。 中国国家主席习近平的专车驶过白宫西翼外的媒体记者群。 Shawn McCreesh是时报白宫记者，报道特朗普政府新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: “习特会”落幕，中美分歧仍然暗流涌动
description: ZOLAN KANNO-YOUNGS, DAVID E. SANGER2026年9月26日 The state visit by President Xi Jinping of China was full of lavish gestures and polite words, but there were few tangible policy announcements on some of the most pressing issues of modern times, such as artificial intelligence, the future of Taiwan and the war in Iran. 中国国家主席习近平的此次国事访问不乏隆重的礼遇与客套的言辞，但在当今时代一些最为紧迫的议题上——如人工智能、台湾前景以及伊朗战争——却鲜有实质性的政策宣布。 At least in public, President Trump seemed more focused on playing host than challenging his geopolitical rival. 至少在公开场合，特朗普总统似乎更专注于履行东道主之谊，而非向其地缘政治对手发起挑战。 Over tea at the White House with Mr. Xi, Mr. Trump described the summit as “tremendous” and said the two superpowers had made “great strides.” Mr. Xi said he and Mr. Trump had added “new substance” to the relationship. 在白宫与习近平茶叙时，特朗普称此次峰会“非常成功”，并表示这两个超级大国已取得“巨大跨越”。习近平则表示，他与特朗普“丰富了”两国关系的“内涵”。 But after nearly two days of meetings, the leaders of the world’s two largest economies and artificial intelligence superpowers had little to show beyond the pageantry. 然而，除了盛大的排场之外，在历时近两天的会谈之后，这两位全球最大经济体兼人工智能超级大国的领导人几乎未能拿出任何实质成果。 Gone were the days when Mr. Trump used meetings with the Chinese leader to celebrate big business deals, like purchases of soybeans and Boeings. Instead, he stressed how well he and Mr. Xi get along, as if that were a shield to questions about Chinese companies aiding Iran with satellite imagery that it has used to mount attacks in the region, or the rapid growth of its nuclear weapons program or its territorial declarations in the South China Sea. 特朗普过去利用与中国领导人的会晤来庆祝大额商业订单（如采购大豆和波音飞机）的日子已一去不复返。取而代之的是，他极力强调自己与习近平相处融洽，仿佛这能成为挡箭牌，规避外界对中国企业向伊朗提供卫星图像协助其在该地区发动袭击、中国核武器计划迅猛扩张以及中国在南海的领土主张等问题的质疑。 “Trump has increasingly collapsed the vast challenge of U.S.-China relations into the narrow question of his personal relationship with Xi,” said Julian Gewirtz, a former China director for the National Security Council in the Biden administration and now a research scholar at Columbia University. “He seems either unaware of or unconcerned by Beijing’s effort to turn today’s stabilization into tomorrow’s constraints on U.S. policy.” “特朗普日益将美中关系的宏大挑战简化为其与习近平个人关系这一狭义问题，”拜登政府时期国家安全委员会前中国事务主任、现哥伦比亚大学研究学者朱利安·格维茨表示。“对于北京试图将眼下的局势稳定转化为未来对美国政策的钳制，他似乎要么浑然不知，要么漠不关心。” 周五，彭丽媛与梅拉尼娅·特朗普在白宫与各自的丈夫习近平和特朗普一同茶叙。 Mr. Trump showed the Chinese leader the construction of the White House helipad and ballroom. He presented Mr. Xi a statue of a bald eagle as American tech titans dined on sea bass. And even as the White House runs a taxpayer-funded advertisement condemning communism, Mr. Trump took the leader of China on a tour of the National Archives to see the founding documents of American democracy. 特朗普陪同中国领导人参观了白宫直升机停机坪和宴会厅的施工现场。在美国科技巨头品尝海鲈鱼之际，他向习近平赠送了一尊白头鹰雕像。甚至在白宫投放由纳税人资助的广告谴责共产主义的同时，特朗普还陪同中国领导人参观了国家档案馆，观看了美国民主的立国文献。 In many ways, the summit between Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi was more notable for what they appeared to avoid detailing rather than what they did announce. 在很大程度上，特朗普与习近平之间的这场峰会值得关注之处更多在于双方似乎刻意回避详述的内容，而非他们实际公布的成果。 Of course, the administration could announce some progress in the days ahead. When asked if the visit had produced additional policy plans, the White House referred to one of Mr. Trump’s social media posts describing the visit as “one of Friendship, Strength, and Success.” “Much has been, and will be, accomplished,” Mr. Trump said without providing details. 当然，美国政府可能会在未来几天公布一些进展。当被问及此次访问是否产生了更多政策成果时，白宫建议媒体参考特朗普发表的一条社交媒体动态。在该贴文中，特朗普将这次访问描述为“展现友谊、实力与成功之旅”。“许多工作已经完成，更多成果在后头，”特朗普在未提供具体细节的情况下如是说道。 Mr. Trump’s aides and supporters say his personal relationship is key to his diplomatic approach with China. 特朗普的幕僚与支持者指出，私交是他开展对华外交策略的核心关键。 The two nations did agree to extend, briefly, a trade truce reached in October 2025 during a meeting in South Korea. That deal had eased an intensifying economic confrontation, during which Mr. Trump imposed tariffs that briefly reached 145 percent, and Mr. Xi suspended most exports of critical minerals and magnets. 双方确实同意短暂延长2025年10月在韩国会晤期间达成的贸易休战协议。该协议曾在一定程度上缓解了不断升温的经济对抗；在对抗期间，特朗普一度加征高达145%的关税，而习近平则暂停了绝大多数关键矿物与磁体的出口。 The accord, set to expire in November, was extended by two months. Mr. Trump said his efforts with Mr. Xi would also be “great for the farmers” but neither side gave any details. China had agreed to sharply increase its purchases of American agricultural products when the two leaders last met, but there is little sign Beijing has made good on the promise. 这项原定于11月到期的协议获展期两个月。特朗普声称他与习近平的沟通也将“对广大农民大有裨益”，但双方均未透露任何细节。两国领导人上次会晤时，中国曾同意大幅增加对美农产品的采购，但几乎没有迹象表明北京兑现了承诺。 特朗普陪同一名共产主义政权领导人参观美国国家档案馆，并观看了《独立宣言》。 There were no new announcements on how to rein in artificial intelligence, even after a summer in which A.I. agents broke out of the “sandboxes” where they were being tested, conducted cyberattacks on their own and covered their tracks. Mr. Trump had short-circuited the discussion using social media to declare that A.I. “will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is,” posting hours before Mr. Xi arrived. “That is China’s position also.” 尽管在此前的夏季中，AI智能体曾突破测试“沙盒”并自主发起网络攻击且掩盖踪迹，但本次会晤并未就如何约束人工智能出台新举措。早在习近平抵达前数小时，特朗普便通过社交平台发文打断了该议题的讨论，声称人工智能“固然是重要议题，但我希望维持现状”，并补充称“这也是中国的立场”。 But the Chinese leader, in his opening statement, emphasized the need for “human control” over A.I. agents, a topic Mr. Trump has avoided. It is still unclear whether they discussed the subject at any length in private. 然而中国领导人在开场致辞中，强调了对AI智能体保持“人类控制”的必要性，而这一话题正是特朗普所刻意回避的。双方是否在闭门会谈中深入探讨了该议题，目前仍不得而知。 Much the same mystery surrounds their talks on Taiwan. Mr. Trump told reporters on the way back from his trip to China in May that he would soon decide on a new arms package for Taiwan, after consulting Taiwan’s “leader,” presumably a reference to President Lai Ching-te. Such a consultation would have been a breach of the rules in how to deal with the island territory, which China claims as its own, and there is no evidence that it happened. Mr. Trump never made public a decision. 双方关于台湾问题的会谈同样笼罩在迷雾之中。特朗普在5月访华归程中曾向媒体表示，他在咨询台湾“领导人”（推测指赖清德）后，将很快就对台新军售案作出决定。此种协商本会违背处理该岛屿领土（中国声明拥有其主权）的交往惯例，且并无证据表明此类协商确实发生过。特朗普也始终未公开任何决定。 Mr. Xi pressed Mr. Trump to oppose Taiwan independence, according to a Chinese readout of their meetings. (To shape the narrative, China turned out its version of the discussions almost immediately.) 根据中方发布的会谈通稿，习近平敦促特朗普明确反对“台独”。（为了引导舆论叙事，中方几乎在会后第一时间发布了其版本的会谈情况。） 特朗普向习近平展示他在白宫新建的直升机停机坪。 Mr. Trump appears to have not given him any commitments. David Purdue, the U.S. ambassador to China, told CNBC there had been no change in the administration’s approach to Taiwan. 特朗普似乎并未做出任何承诺。美国驻华大使庞德伟(David Purdue)向CNBC表示，本届政府在台湾问题上的既定政策并未发生改变。 Allen R. Carlson, a professor at Cornell University who focuses on U.S.-China relations and Asia security, said Mr. Trump’s apparent refusal to acquiesce to Mr. Xi’s demands on Taiwan could be viewed as “good news for America’s standing and for the island.” 康奈尔大学关注美中关系与亚洲安全的教授艾伦·R·卡尔森指出，特朗普显然拒绝默许习近平在台湾问题上的诉求，这可被视为“对美国的国际威望以及台湾方面的利好消息”。 But he said it is also a sign of the low expectations for the summit. 但他也表示，这同样折射出外界对此次峰会的期望值普遍偏低。 “We are now relieved when an American president simply declines to narrow a commitment that has stood for forty years,” Mr. Carlson said. “His silence will be counted in some corners as an American win. In reality the game and set go to Beijing, if not yet the match.” “如今只要美国总统没有削弱一项延续了四十年的承诺，我们竟就会感到如释重负，”卡尔森表示。“他的沉默在某些阵营看来将被奉为美国的胜利。但现实是，即便尚未输掉整场比赛，这一局和这一盘的赢家也是北京。” Mr. Xi came armed with the ultimate soft-power diplomatic gesture. He announced a decision to send two pandas to the Atlanta zoo and committed to accepting tens of thousands of additional American exchange students in China in the coming years. But that was reaching into an old playbook for Chinese leaders. 习近平此次展现了极具代表性的软实力外交姿态。他宣布将向亚特兰大动物园运送两只大熊猫，并承诺在未来几年内额外接收上万名美国交换生赴华学习。然而，这不过是沿用了中国领导人的传统策略。 The two are expected to meet again this year. Mr. Trump told Mr. Xi that he would be attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, in November. He later added that Mr. Xi agreed to attend the Group of 20 summit in Florida in December. “I look forward to our next meeting!” Mr. Trump said on social media. 预计双方年内还将再次会晤。特朗普向习近平表示，他将出席11月在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会。他随后补充称，习近平已同意出席12月在佛罗里达州举行的二十国集团峰会。“期待我们的下一次聚会！”特朗普在社交平台上写道。 Mr. Trump insisted on social media that the meetings with Mr. Xi were “very productive.” 特朗普在社交媒体上强调，与习近平的会晤“富有建设性”。 The one example he cited in that post was Mr. Xi’s seemingly supporting his rebrand of artificial intelligence as “super intelligence.” 他在该帖文中举出的唯一例证，是习近平似乎赞同他将人工智能改称为“超级智能”(super intelligence)。 “That would be ‘SUPER!’” Mr. Trump said. “那真是‘超’棒！”特朗普写道。 Zolan Kanno-Young是时报白宫记者，报道特朗普总统及其政府。 David E. Sanger报道特朗普政府和一系列国家安全问题。他在时报任职超过40年，著有四本关于美国国家安全挑战的书。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

Carlson, a professor at Cornell University who focuses on U.S.-China relations and Asia security, said Mr. Trump’s apparent refusal to acquiesce to Mr. Xi’s demands on Taiwan could be viewed as “good news for America’s standing and for the island.” 康奈尔大学关注美中关系与亚洲安全的教授艾伦·R·卡尔森指出，特朗普显然拒绝默许习近平在台湾问题上的诉求，这可被视为“对美国的国际威望以及台湾方面的利好消息”。 But he said it is also a sign of the low expectations for the summit. 但他也表示，这同样折射出外界对此次峰会的期望值普遍偏低。 “We are now relieved when an American president simply declines to narrow a commitment that has stood for forty years,” Mr. Carlson said. “His silence will be counted in some corners as an American win. In reality the game and set go to Beijing, if not yet the match.” “如今只要美国总统没有削弱一项延续了四十年的承诺，我们竟就会感到如释重负，”卡尔森表示。“他的沉默在某些阵营看来将被奉为美国的胜利。但现实是，即便尚未输掉整场比赛，这一局和这一盘的赢家也是北京。” Mr. Xi came armed with the ultimate soft-power diplomatic gesture. He announced a decision to send two pandas to the Atlanta zoo and committed to accepting tens of thousands of additional American exchange students in China in the coming years. But that was reaching into an old playbook for Chinese leaders. 习近平此次展现了极具代表性的软实力外交姿态。他宣布将向亚特兰大动物园运送两只大熊猫，并承诺在未来几年内额外接收上万名美国交换生赴华学习。然而，这不过是沿用了中国领导人的传统策略。 The two are expected to meet again this year. Mr. Trump told Mr. Xi that he would be attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, in November. He later added that Mr. Xi agreed to attend the Group of 20 summit in Florida in December. “I look forward to our next meeting!” Mr. Trump said on social media. 预计双方年内还将再次会晤。特朗普向习近平表示，他将出席11月在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会。他随后补充称，习近平已同意出席12月在佛罗里达州举行的二十国集团峰会。“期待我们的下一次聚会！”特朗普在社交平台上写道。 Mr. Trump insisted on social media that the meetings with Mr. Xi were “very productive.” 特朗普在社交媒体上强调，与习近平的会晤“富有建设性”。 The one example he cited in that post was Mr. Xi’s seemingly supporting his rebrand of artificial intelligence as “super intelligence.” 他 在该帖文中举出的 唯一例证，是习近平似乎赞同他将人工智能改称为“超级智能”(super intelligence)。 “That would be ‘SUPER!’” Mr. Trump said. “那真是‘超’棒！”特朗普写道。 Zolan Kanno-Young 是时报白宫记者，报道特朗普总统及其政府。 David E. Sanger 报道特朗普政府和一系列国家安全问题。他在时报任职超过40年，著有四本关于美国国家安全挑战的书。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: paperclipai/paperclip
description: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work https://paperclip.ing Quickstart · Docs · GitHub · Discord · Twitter · Website Paperclip is the app people use to manage AI agents for work. Open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents. If OpenClaw is an employee, Paperclip is the company. Paperclip is a Node.js server and React UI that orchestrates a team of AI agents to run a business. Bring your own agents, assign goals, and track work and costs from one dashboard. It looks like a task manager. Under the hood: org charts, budgets, governance, goal alignment, and agent coordination. Manage business goals, not pull requests. Step Example 01 Define the goal "Build the #1 AI note-taking app to $1M MRR." 02 Hire the team CEO, CTO, engineers, designers, marketers — any bot, any provider. 03 Approve and run Review strategy. Set budgets. Hit go. Monitor from the dashboard. Works with OpenClaw Claude Code Codex Cursor Bash HTTP If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired. Paperclip is right for you if ✅ You want to build autonomous AI organizations ✅ You coordinate many different agents (OpenClaw, Codex, Claude, Cursor) toward a common goal ✅ You have 20 simultaneous Claude Code terminals open and lose track of what everyone is doing ✅ You want agents running autonomously 24/7, but still want to audit work and chime in when needed ✅ You want to monitor costs and enforce budgets ✅ You want a process for managing agents that feels like using a task manager ✅ You want to manage your autonomous businesses from your phone The four pillars Four things have to work for an organization of AI agents to actually produce: the tasks, the org, the training, and the infrastructure. Paperclip is built around exactly those four pillars. Pillar Built for What it covers Agentic Task Manager — Declare intent. Agents work. You verify the output. Everyone, daily Tasks, approvals & review gates · proactive agent coworkers · auditable routines & workflows · verify from diffs, screenshots & tests Org Chart for Agents — Roles, permissions & boundaries for humans and agents. Managers Mixed human + agent org chart · responsibilities, delegation, specialization · governance: who can do what · scoped secrets & company boundaries Agent Employee Training — Design, train & evaluate your AI employees. Enablers Skill Studio & shared org-wide skills · evals & saved test runs · active learning loops & quality metrics · performance reviews for agents Agentic OS — The infrastructure that makes the work run. IT & platform Cross-provider runtime: any model, any agent · sandboxing, integrations & MCP servers · SSO, GRC, RBAC & cost controls · data privacy, internal trace collection, compounding data value Features 🔌 Bring Your Own Agent Any agent, any runtime, one org chart. If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired. 🎯 Goal Alignment Every task traces back to the organization mission. Agents know what to do and why. 💓 Heartbeats Agents wake on a schedule, check work, and act. Delegation flows up and down the org chart. 💰 Cost Control Monthly budgets per agent. When they hit the limit, they stop. No runaway costs. 🏢 Multi-Organization One deployment, many organizations. Complete data isolation. One control plane for your portfolio. 🎫 Ticket System Every conversation traced. Every decision explained. Full tool-call tracing and immutable audit log. 🛡️ Governance Approve hires, override strategy, pause or terminate any agent — at any time. 📊 Org Chart Hierarchies, roles, reporting lines. Your agents have a boss, a title, and a job description. 📱 Mobile Ready Monitor and manage your autonomous businesses from anywhere. Problems Paperclip solves Without Paperclip With Paperclip ❌ You have 20 Claude Code tabs open and can't track which one does what. On reboot you lose everything. ✅ Tasks are ticket-based, conversations are threaded, sessions persist across reboots. ❌ You manually gather context from several places to remind your bot what you're actually doing. ✅ Context flows from the task up through the project and company goals — your agent always knows what to do and why. ❌ Folders of agent configs are disorganized and you're re-inventing task management, communication, and coordination between agents. ✅ Paperclip gives you org charts, ticketing, delegation, and governance out of the box — so you run a company, not a pile of scripts. ❌ Runaway loops waste hundreds of dollars of tokens and max your quota before you even know what happened. ✅ Cost tracking surfaces token budgets and throttles agents when they're out. Management prioritizes with budgets. ❌ You have recurring jobs (customer support, social, reports) and have to remember to manually kick them off. ✅ Heartbeats handle regular work on a schedule. Management supervises. ❌ You have an idea, you have to find your repo, fire up Claude Code, keep a tab open, and babysit it. ✅ Add a task in Paperclip. Your coding agent works on it until it's done. Management reviews their work. Why Paperclip is special Paperclip handles the hard orchestration details correctly. Atomic execution. Task checkout and budget enforcement are atomic, so no double-work and no runaway spend. Persistent agent state. Agents resume the same task context across heartbeats instead of restarting from scratch. Runtime skill injection. Agents can learn Paperclip workflows and project context at runtime, without retraining. Governance with rollback. Approval gates are enforced, config changes are revisioned, and bad changes can be rolled back safely. Goal-aware execution. Tasks carry full goal ancestry so agents consistently see the "why," not just a title. Portable company templates. Export/import orgs, agents, and skills with secret scrubbing and collision handling. True multi-organization isolation. Every entity is company-scoped, so one deployment can run many companies with separate data and audit trails. What's Under the Hood Paperclip is a full control plane, not a wrapper. Before you build any of this yourself, know that it already exists: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PAPERCLIP SERVER │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │ │Identity & │ │ Work & │ │ Heartbeat │ │Governance │ │ │ │ Access │ │ Tasks │ │ Execution │ │& Approvals│ │ │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │ │ Org Chart │ │Workspaces │ │ Plugins │ │ Budget │ │ │ │ & Agents │ │ & Runtime │ │ │ │ & Costs │ │ │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │ │ Routines │ │ Secrets & │ │ Activity │ │ Company │ │ │ │& Schedules│ │ Storage │ │ & Events │ │Portability│ │ │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ▲ ▲ ▲ ▲ ┌─────┴─────┐ ┌─────┴─────┐ ┌─────┴─────┐ ┌─────┴─────┐ │ Claude │ │ Codex │ │ CLI │ │ HTTP/web │ │ Code │ │ │ │ agents │ │ bots │ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ The Systems Identity & Access — Two deployment modes (trusted local or authenticated), board users, agent API keys, short-lived run JWTs, company memberships, invite flows, and OpenClaw onboarding. Every mutating request is traced to an actor. Org Chart & Agents — Agents have roles, titles, reporting lines, permissions, and budgets. Adapter examples match the diagram: Claude Code, Codex, CLI agents such as Cursor/Gemini/bash, HTTP/webhook bots such as OpenClaw, and external adapter plugins. If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired. Work & Task System — Issues carry company/project/goal/parent links, atomic checkout with execution locks, first-class blocker dependencies, comments, documents, attachments, work products, labels, and inbox state. No double-work, no lost context. Heartbeat Execution — DB-backed wakeup queue with coalescing, budget checks, workspace resolution, secret injection, skill loading, and adapter invocation. Runs produce structured logs, cost events, session state, and audit trails. Recovery handles orphaned runs automatically. Workspaces & Runtime — Project workspaces, isolated execution workspaces (git worktrees, operator branches), and runtime services (dev servers, preview URLs). Agents work in the right directory with the right context every time. Governance & Approvals — Board approval workflows, execution policies with review/approval stages, decision tracking, budget hard-stops, agent pause/resume/terminate, and full audit logging. Nothing ships without your sign-off. Budget & Cost Control — Token and cost tracking by company, agent, project, goal, issue, provider, and model. Scoped budget policies with warning thresholds and hard stops. Overspend pauses agents and cancels queued work automatically. Routines & Schedules — Recurring tasks with cron, webhook, and API triggers. Concurrency and catch-up policies. Each routine execution creates a tracked issue and wakes the assigned agent — no manual kick-offs needed. Plugins — Instance-wide plugin system with out-of-process workers, capability-gated host services, job scheduling, tool exposure, and UI contributions. Extend Paperclip without forking it. Secrets & Storage — Instance and company secrets, encrypted local storage, provider-backed object storage, attachments, and work products. Sensitive values stay out of prompts unless a scoped run explicitly needs them. Activity & Events — Mutating actions, heartbeat state changes, cost events, approvals, comments, and work products are recorded as durable activity so operators can audit what happened and why. Company Portability — Export and import entire organizations — agents, skills, projects, routines, and issues — with secret scrubbing and collision handling. One deployment, many companies, complete data isolation. What Paperclip is not Not a chatbot. Agents have jobs, not chat windows. Not an agent framework. We don't tell you how to build agents. We tell you how to run a company made of them. Not a workflow builder. No drag-and-drop pipelines. Paperclip models companies — with org charts, goals, budgets, and governance. Not a prompt manager. Agents bring their own prompts, models, and runtimes. Paperclip manages the organization they work in. Not a single-agent tool. This is for teams. If you have one agent, you probably don't need Paperclip. If you have twenty — you definitely do. Not a code review tool. Paperclip orchestrates work, not pull requests. Bring your own review process. Quickstart Open source. Self-hosted. No Paperclip account required. curl -fsSLO https://paperclip.ing/install.sh curl -fsSLO https://paperclip.ing/install.sh.sha256 if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum -c install.sh.sha256 else shasum -a 256 -c install.sh.sha256 fi bash install.sh The installer ensures Node.js 24.11 or newer is available, installs a managed Paperclip CLI under ~/.paperclip/cli, and starts interactive onboarding. It can also install Paperclip as a background service on supported Linux and macOS systems. The checksum detects transfer or publishing mistakes, but it is served from the same origin as the script; use a release-tag or commit-pinned GitHub copy when you need an independently hosted source. For a non-interactive managed install: curl -fsSL https://paperclip.ing/install.sh | bash -s -- --no-prompt --no-onboard paperclipai onboard --yes The piped form requires supported Node.js, npm, and npx to already be present. If Node.js bootstrap is required, download and review install.sh before running it so no privileged dependency-install command is accepted through a pipe. To try Paperclip without installing anything permanently: npx --registry https://registry.npmjs.org paperclipai onboard --yes For an isolated manual test instance that is already initialized with a CEO agent, use test-drive. It stays in the foreground, never installs a service or creates a first task, and opens the browser only after setup succeeds: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... npx paperclipai test-drive OPENAI_API_KEY=... npx paperclipai test-drive --harness codex OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... npx paperclipai test-drive \ --harness opencode \ --model openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 Each run without --data-dir gets a unique, retained temporary directory; its absolute path is printed at startup. Pass --data-dir to reuse one, or --no-browser to leave the initialized instance unopened. When invoked from a linked Git worktree, test-drive also enables task execution in that worktree. See doc/CLI.md for credential and reuse behavior. Troubleshooting: private npm registry .npmrc If this fails with an E404 for paperclipai (or similar) and you use a private npm registry (for example GitHub Packages) via a global ~/.npmrc, npx may be resolving paperclipai against that private registry instead of the public npm registry. Diagnostic: npm config get registry Workaround (cross-platform; force the public npm registry for this command): npx --registry https://registry.npmjs.org paperclipai onboard --yes That quickstart path now defaults to trusted local loopback mode for the fastest first run. To start in authenticated/private mode instead, choose a bind preset explicitly: paperclipai onboard --yes --bind lan # or: paperclipai onboard --yes --bind tailnet If you already have Paperclip configured, rerunning onboard keeps the existing config in place. Use paperclipai configure to edit settings. See doc/INSTALLING.md for pinned versions, canary and git-ref installs, updates, rollback, service management, and uninstalling. Or manually: git clone https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip.git cd paperclip pnpm install pnpm dev This starts the API server at http://localhost:3100. An embedded PostgreSQL database is created automatically — no setup required. Requirements: Node.js 24.11+, pnpm 9.15+ FAQ What does a typical setup look like? Locally, a single Node.js process manages an embedded Postgres and local file storage. For production, point it at your own Postgres and deploy however you like. Configure projects, agents, and goals — the agents take care of the rest. If you're a solo entrepreneur you can use Tailscale to access Paperclip on the go. Then later you can deploy to e.g. Vercel when you need it. Can I run multiple companies? Yes. A single deployment can run an unlimited number of companies with complete data isolation. How is Paperclip different from agents like OpenClaw or Claude Code? Paperclip uses those agents. It orchestrates them into a company — with org charts, budgets, goals, governance, and accountability. Why should I use Paperclip instead of just pointing my OpenClaw to Asana or Trello? Agent orchestration has subtleties in how you coordinate who has work checked out, how to maintain sessions, monitoring costs, establishing governance - Paperclip does this for you. (Bring-your-own-ticket-system is on the Roadmap) Do agents run continuously? By default, agents run on scheduled heartbeats and event-based triggers (task assignment, @-mentions). You can also hook in continuous agents like OpenClaw. You bring your agent and Paperclip coordinates. Development pnpm dev # Full dev (API + UI, watch mode) pnpm dev:once # Full dev without file watching pnpm dev:server # Server only pnpm dev:mobile # Serve prebuilt UI on :3101 for phones/tablets (proxies /api → :3100) pnpm dev:both # Run `pnpm dev` and `pnpm dev:mobile` together pnpm build # Build all pnpm typecheck # Type checking pnpm test # Cheap default test run (Vitest only) pnpm test:watch # Vitest watch mode pnpm test:e2e # Playwright browser suite pnpm db:generate # Generate DB migration pnpm db:migrate # Apply migrations pnpm test does not run Playwright. Browser suites stay separate and are typically run only when working on those flows or in CI. See doc/DEVELOPING.md for the full development guide. Roadmap ✅ Plugin system (e.g. add a knowledge base, custom tracing, queues, etc) ✅ Get OpenClaw / claw-style agent employees ✅ companies.sh - import and export entire organizations ✅ Easy AGENTS.md configurations ✅ Skills Manager, Skill Studio & Skills Store ✅ Scheduled Routines ✅ Better Budgeting ✅ Agent Reviews and Approvals ✅ Multiple Human Users ✅ Cloud / Sandbox agents (e2b, Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, Novita, self-hosted Kubernetes) ✅ Artifacts & Work Products ✅ Deep Planning (planning mode, revisioned plans, plan approvals) ✅ Enforced Outcomes (watchdogs, recovery actions, review gates) ✅ MCP Tool Gateway & Apps (governed tool access) ✅ Secrets Manager with per-agent access ✅ Activity log & action attribution ✅ Self-healing runs & automatic recovery ✅ Agent evals & feedback ⚪ Memory / Knowledge ⚪ MAXIMIZER MODE ⚪ Work Queues ⚪ Self-Organization ⚪ Automatic Organizational Learning ⚪ CEO Chat 🟡 Cloud deployments (multi-tenant isolation & company Import/Export shipped) ⚪ Desktop App ⚪ Bring-your-own-ticket-system (Asana / Linear / Jira as on-ramps) ⚪ Connected Apps (one-click integrations, e.g. Vercel) This is the short roadmap preview. See the full roadmap in ROADMAP.md. Community & Plugins Find Plugins and more at awesome-paperclip Observability Paperclip ships with opt-in OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation for the server (traces only). It activates when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set and supports grpc, http/protobuf, and http/json via the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL env var. @opentelemetry/api is a normal server dependency; the SDK, auto-instrumentation, and exporter packages are optional peer dependencies — install them only if you want tracing. See doc/observability.md for install commands and the full env-var reference. Paperclip also ships with opt-in Sentry error monitoring for the server and the browser. Set SENTRY_DSN_FRONTEND to activate it for the browser and SENTRY_DSN_BACKEND to activate it for the server — each variable is optional, and the legacy SENTRY_DSN variable still works as a fallback for either component. The supported server SDK version is @sentry/node@10.71.0; it is an optional peer dependency for the server, so install it only if you want error monitoring. The browser SDK, @sentry/browser, is pinned to the same exact version. See doc/observability.md for the install command, the privacy settings, and the full default capture set. Telemetry Paperclip collects anonymous usage telemetry to help us understand how the product is used and improve it. No personal information, issue content, prompts, file paths, or secrets are ever collected. Private repository references are hashed with a per-install salt before being sent. Contributors changing emitted telemetry events should follow the Telemetry Data Contract. For proposed first-party events that are not in the generated contract yet, follow Telemetry Workflow. Telemetry is enabled by default and can be disabled with any of the following: Method How Environment variable PAPERCLIP_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 Standard convention DO_NOT_TRACK=1 CI environments Automatically disabled when CI=true Config file Set telemetry.enabled: false in your Paperclip config Contributing We welcome contributions. See the contributing guide for details. Community Discord — Join the community Twitter / X — Follow updates and announcements GitHub Issues — bugs and feature requests GitHub Discussions — ideas and RFC License MIT © 2026 Paperclip Labs, Inc Star History Open source under MIT. Built for people who want to get work done, not babysit agents.
